speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You presented with gait and limb ataxia; to begin our investigation, have you noticed any other neurological symptoms like double vision, difficulty speaking, or weakness in your arms and legs?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the clumsiness on your right side is a helpful clue. To understand if this is part of a progressive condition, have you noticed any changes in your handwriting, your speech patterns, or your balance when standing still?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.

Given your history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab, the new onset of right-sided limb and gait ataxia is highly suspicious for PML, an opportunistic infection of the central nervous system. Please confirm if you have noticed any visual field defects or subtle changes in your vision recently, as this is a common presenting symptom.
